dimensions.name: Spec comprehension & format reconnaissance

evidence.note: Before writing any decoder code, the agent walked the RFC table of contents (step 5) and systematically read every relevant section by line range — frame header, blocks, literals, sequences, sequence execution, FSE table construction, Huffman tree/weights, dictionary format, and Appendix A predefined tables — extracting the tricky ones (FSE, Huffman weights, Appendix A, dictionary) to /tmp files for reference. This is genuine section-by-section reconnaissance, not reactive skimming.

Repeatedly dumped real .zst inputs with `od` and manually parsed the bytes against the spec — correctly decoding simple.zst (magic 0xFD2FB528, FHD=0x24 → Single_Segment/checksum flags, 1-byte FCS, raw block) and repetitive.zst (FCS=15322, compressed block, LL=RLE/OF=FSE/ML=RLE modes). Cross-checking hex dumps of real frames against the RFC is the hallmark of anchor 8.

Anticipated subsystem interactions from the reading — flagged treeless literal reuse, dictionary preloaded entropy/offset state (magic 0xEC30A437), repeat-offset LL=0, and reverse-direction bitstreams before implementing them, showing an internalized whole-format model.

Comprehension gaps surfaced: the predefined ML/OF tables were initially filled with placeholder/sequential values and the offset table had wrong/missing entries, forcing re-reads of Appendix A to correct them. Field-width/table errors like these are exactly the 'subtly wrong' failures the dimension warns about — internalization was imperfect.

Bit-ordering rules were mis-read and flip-flopped across several rewrites (whether to reverse bits within bytes, initial FSE state read order LL/OF/ML, stop-bit detection). Persistent uncertainty about the exact bit-level contract shows the model was not verified up front, keeping this below anchor 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it read the relevant RFC sections systematically before implementing each subsystem and repeatedly grounded understanding in hex dumps of real frames (anchor-8 behavior at steps 18-19,29,35). It also anticipated tricky interactions (treeless reuse, dictionary state) from the reading. But it falls short of a clean 8/10 because internalization was imperfect — predefined tables were entered as placeholders and bit-ordering/state-order rules were repeatedly mis-read and reversed, requiring multiple corrective RFC re-reads rather than a precise verified model. That places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & build ordering

evidence.note: Implemented frame parse + raw block first and verified simple.zst decodes to 'test' before moving on — a walking-skeleton first milestone with a concrete done-signal.

Plans repeatedly enumerate subsystems in correct dependency order (literals types, sequences modes, FSE tables, sequence execution/repeat offsets, dictionary), showing dependency-aware decomposition in the agent's head.

Rather than landing subsystems incrementally, wrote one 'comprehensive implementation' covering literals/sequences/FSE/Huffman/dictionary at once — a monolithic push that undercuts clean milestone separation.

img.png.zst (raw block) verified as a second done-signal; step 81 plan lays out an explicit ordered milestone sequence mapping input classes to features (test repetitive → run all → Huffman literals → dictionary).

Got stuck debugging the compressed/FSE/sequences path (repetitive.zst) for the entire back half; Huffman-literals and dictionary milestones were listed but never reached or verified as isolated done-conditions.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed a sensible dependency-ordered decomposition and a genuine raw-blocks-first walking skeleton with concrete input-class done-signals (simple.zst, img.png.zst), plus explicit ordered plans mapping later features to input classes — traits between anchors 5 and 8. However, after the raw milestone it wrote a single monolithic 'comprehensive' implementation covering all remaining subsystems at once (step 49) and then bogged down on FSE/sequences without ever landing Huffman or dictionary as separate verified milestones, keeping it short of the explicit, cleanly-separated milestone structure of anchor 8. This lands at 6.

dimensions.name: Differential-testing & correctness verification

evidence.note: Checked `which zstd` and found none installed; never established or improvised any reference-decoder comparison, so no differential testing occurred.
Verification consisted of running the binary on provided simple.zst/repetitive.zst and eyeballing output — success judged by whether it matched the hex-derived 'test' string or returned 0 bytes.
Same loop repeated against the fixed set of provided artifacts (repetitive, img.png, audio.wav); no self-generated inputs, no feature-matrix corpus, no automated byte-exact diff.
Lone `md5sum` attempt to inspect output failed (tool unavailable); no other automated correctness check was set up.
test.sh was only `cat`'d once and referenced in plans but never actually executed as a verification step.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's correctness checking never rose above running the binary on the handful of provided .zst artifacts and eyeballing byte counts / a manually-derived expected string — squarely anchor 0 behavior ('runs the binary and eyeballs output'). It never even executed the provided test.sh (below anchor 3), generated no inputs of its own, and built no differential or automated byte-exact comparison harness (well below anchor 5), partly because no reference zstd/python existed and it made no attempt to work around that. I place it at 1: marginally above pure 'it compiles' only because it systematically ran multiple provided inputs and manually compared one known output.

dimensions.name: Feature-coverage tracking & stuck detection

evidence.note: Maintains a rough, prose-level list of features done vs. remaining and correctly maps which test files exercise which features (raw blocks work; repetitive needs sequences; other files need Huffman literals; dictionary still to do).
Clearly aware it is repeatedly failing on the same input (repetitive.zst returns 0/8 bytes) and keeps returning to it — the 'notices repeated failure' behavior of anchor 5.

Circular debugging: repeatedly declares 'found the bug' with a new single-cause diagnosis (predefined tables → bit reversal → initial-state order → sequence order → bit-reader shift) that each fails, rather than stepping back to a fundamentally different verification tactic.

Does vary tactic somewhat — builds a debug instrumented version and extraction scripts — showing more than blind retrying, nudging above pure 5 but not reaching the sustained re-diagnosis of anchor 8.

Plans repeatedly promise 'then run test.sh / test all files' but the run never happens; trajectory ends still stuck on the first compressed file with only two raw-block inputs verified — coverage map stays implicit and unreconciled.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent keeps a rough prose checklist of the feature matrix and knows which inputs test what, and it plainly notices it is repeatedly failing on repetitive.zst — squarely matching anchor 5. It varies diagnostic tactics (debug builds, extraction scripts, RFC re-reads), which edges toward 6, but it never truly steps back to re-diagnose: it issues a string of premature 'found the bug' declarations that each patch a different symptom, never runs test.sh to snapshot coverage, and its coverage picture stays implicit and unreconciled. That falls short of the explicit, accurate, self-correcting map described at anchor 8, placing it at 5.

dimensions.name: Root-causing & course-correction on mismatches

evidence.note: Traced repetitive.zst's 0-byte output to a real earlier-code bug: ml_predef FSE table filled with placeholder sequential values. Re-read Appendix A and corrected it — genuine root-cause of a falsified earlier assumption, not a symptom patch.
Found table-size errors (66/67 entries vs required 64) and the subtle 'state-0 termination entry' rule, correcting the underlying table logic by re-reading the RFC clause.

Added debug printf and used state->symbol tracing ('OF state 30 decodes to symbol 23, should be 25') to localize the wrong subsystem — a step toward hex/state-level pinpointing characteristic of the higher anchor.
Revised earlier subsystems (sequence read order, stop-bit detection, br_fill bit-reader shift direction) when new bugs revealed wrong earlier assumptions — willingness to revisit prior code.

Bit-reversal logic flip-flopped (remove -> re-add -> 'found the real bug'), and changes were bundled several-at-once, showing guessing rather than isolated hypothesis testing; never converged on repetitive.zst across ~35 debug steps.
Asserts 'our current code does this correctly' while the OF symbol is still wrong, showing lingering unresolved confusion and non-convergence at the trajectory's end.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently localizes bugs to the correct subsystem (predefined tables, bit reader, sequence order), re-reads the governing RFC sections when fixes fail, adds state-level debug tracing, and revises earlier code when assumptions are falsified — clearly exceeding symptom-patching (anchor 3) and matching or slightly exceeding anchor 5. It reaches toward anchor 8 via state->symbol tracing and cross-subsystem revision, but the execution is noisy: bit-reversal logic oscillates, multiple hypotheses change per rewrite without isolation, and it never converges on the target input. That places it at a 6 — solid subsystem localization with partial, undisciplined byte-level tracing, short of the isolated hypothesis-driven convergence of the top anchors.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity task: implement a complete Zstandard decoder in C purely from RFC 8878, producing byte-identical output to `zstd -d` across the full feature matrix (frame headers, three block types, all literal encodings, FSE in four modes, Huffman with FSE weights + treeless reuse, sequence machinery with repeat-offset history, multi-frame and dictionary frames). Difficulty comes from a dense binary spec that must be understood precisely, many interdependent subsystems that must be built in the right order, and correctness that is bit-exact and unforgiving — a single misread field breaks everything downstream. This warrants heavy, sustained meta-work: careful spec orientation, layered decomposition with per-component checks, a differential-testing verification strategy against the reference tool, tight progress tracking across dozens of features, and disciplined course-correction when a mis-decoded field surfaces far from its cause.

dimensions.name: Spec comprehension & format reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Reading and correctly internalizing the relevant sections of RFC 8878 before and while implementing each subsystem, and probing real .zst inputs to ground understanding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The only source of truth is a dense binary-format spec; every field width, bit order, and table-construction rule must be read precisely. Acting from a half-remembered mental model of zstd (rather than the actual RFC text) produces subtly wrong decoders that fail bit-exact comparison in ways that are extremely hard to diagnose later.

anchors.0: Starts coding from prior/assumed knowledge of zstd; never meaningfully consults the RFC or inspects sample inputs.
anchors.3: Skims the RFC for the current feature only, reactively, and often mis-reads bit-ordering / field-width details; no examination of actual byte layouts.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant RFC section before implementing each subsystem and gets most field definitions right; occasionally dumps bytes of a sample frame to confirm structure.
anchors.8: Systematically works the RFC section by section, extracts the exact rules for tricky areas (FSE table build, Huffman weight decoding, repeat-offset LL=0 case, window/FCS field widths) and cross-checks them against hex dumps of real frames before trusting the implementation.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, verified model of the whole format up front and deepens it per subsystem: reconciles ambiguous spec passages against observed bytes, anticipates the interactions (treeless literal reuse, dictionary-preloaded entropy/offset state) from the reading, and documents the exact bit-level contract so later debugging traces cleanly back to spec clauses.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & build ordering
dimensions.description: Breaking the decoder into an ordered hierarchy of independently-checkable components (frame parse → block dispatch → literals → FSE → Huffman → sequences → offset history → dictionaries) with an explicit done-condition for each.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The subsystems have hard dependencies (sequences need FSE; Huffman literals need FSE weights; dictionaries preload entropy state). Building in the wrong order, or as one monolithic push, means nothing is verifiable until everything is done — fatal on a task this size.

anchors.0: Treats it as one undifferentiated coding effort; no visible sub-goals or ordering.
anchors.3: Vague ordering in the agent's head; components entangled so none can be tested alone; milestones are just 'write more code'.
anchors.5: Clear list of the major subsystems tackled in a sensible dependency order, each landed before moving on, with an implicit 'this feature works now' checkpoint.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone structure that respects dependencies and picks a walking-skeleton path (e.g. raw blocks / raw literals end-to-end first, then FSE, then Huffman, then sequences, then dictionaries), each milestone with a concrete done-signal (a class of inputs now decodes correctly).
anchors.10: A layered plan that sequences by both dependency and diagnostic isolation — earliest features chosen to make later ones debuggable, each subsystem given its own smallest-possible test input, and the plan re-ordered deliberately when an unexpected dependency (e.g. offset history spanning blocks) is discovered.

dimensions.name: Differential-testing & correctness verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing how correctness is checked — differential comparison against `zstd -d`, per-subsystem and per-input-shape test coverage, byte-exact diffs — beyond the provided `test.sh` sanity check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Correctness is bit-exact and the visible `test.sh` covers only a handful of inputs; the grading set exercises every feature. An agent that leans only on test.sh will believe it is done while whole feature classes (8-byte FCS, treeless literals, dictionary frames, overlapping match copies) are silently broken.

anchors.0: No verification beyond 'it compiles'; or runs the binary and eyeballs output.
anchors.3: Relies solely on the provided test.sh; treats passing it as done.
anchors.5: Generates a few of its own .zst inputs and diffs decoder output against `zstd -d`, covering the common cases beyond test.sh.
anchors.8: Constructs a deliberate differential-testing harness that feeds many inputs — spanning the feature matrix (each FCS width, each block type, each literal/FSE mode, multi-frame, checksum, dictionary) — through both its decoder and `zstd -d` and compares byte-for-byte, using targeted inputs to isolate which subsystem fails.
anchors.10: Systematically enumerates the full feature matrix from the RFC and engineers inputs (or corpora) that exercise each edge — overlapping copies, LL=0 repeat-offset, treeless reuse across blocks, dictionary-preloaded state, skippable frames — with automated byte-exact comparison, adds regression cases as bugs are found, and treats an unexplained mismatch as a first-class signal rather than noise.

dimensions.name: Feature-coverage tracking & stuck detection
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which features work vs remain across the large matrix, and recognizing when debugging a single mismatch has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With dozens of interacting features and bit-exact grading, it is easy to lose the plot — to think the decoder is largely done when several feature classes are untested, or to burn the horizon re-debugging one FSE bug in circles. Accurate self-assessment decides whether the horizon is spent well.

anchors.0: No sense of overall coverage; declares done with large feature classes never exercised; or loops on one bug indefinitely with no awareness.
anchors.3: Tracks progress only implicitly; conflates 'test.sh passes' with 'complete'; little awareness of being stuck.
anchors.5: Keeps a rough checklist of features done vs remaining and notices when repeatedly failing on the same input.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, accurate coverage map of the feature matrix (what is verified, what is untested, what is failing), and when a bug resists, steps back to re-diagnose rather than retrying the same fix.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles claimed-done against verified-done across the whole matrix, flags untested corners honestly, detects circular debugging early and switches diagnostic tactic (narrower input, hex-level trace, re-read spec clause), keeping an accurate done-vs-remaining picture across the entire long build.

dimensions.name: Root-causing & course-correction on mismatches
dimensions.description: When decoded output diverges from the reference, tracing the byte-exact mismatch back to the true faulty subsystem and revising the implementation/understanding, rather than patching symptoms or pressing on.
dimensions.why_it_matters: In a streaming binary decoder, an error in one field (e.g. window size, an FSE state update) manifests as garbage far downstream. Effective decoders demand disciplined root-cause tracing and willingness to revisit the spec and revise earlier code when an assumption is falsified.

anchors.0: Ignores mismatches, or keeps changing code randomly hoping output aligns; barrels ahead on falsified assumptions.
anchors.3: Patches the visible symptom (e.g. special-cases one input) without finding the real cause; fragile fixes accumulate.
anchors.5: Localizes most bugs to the right subsystem and fixes them, occasionally re-reading the spec when a fix doesn't hold.
anchors.8: Uses the byte offset of first divergence and hex-level tracing to pinpoint the responsible field/state, re-reads the governing RFC clause, and corrects the underlying logic — including revising earlier subsystems when a new bug reveals a wrong earlier assumption.
anchors.10: Treats each mismatch as a hypothesis-driven investigation: isolates with a minimal input, traces state to the exact bit, distinguishes a local bug from a mis-modeled contract, and refactors the design when a root cause invalidates prior structure — converging reliably rather than accumulating band-aids across the whole feature set.
